turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's largest SHG tensor
component |d_ij|, then select the 5 candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20
pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the structures

**Step 1 – What controls |d| in the training set**

| structural class | typical |d| (pm/V) |
|---|---|
| Ionic halides / alkali‑chalcogenometallates (closed‑shell, centro‑like cation arrays) | 0.1 – 3 |
| Li/Na‑rich thio‑phosphates, borates, aluminates | 4 – 13 |
| **Defect‑chalcopyrite (II–III₂–S₄) sulfides**: Cd₂Ga₄S₈ 21.7, Al₄Hg₂S₈ 21.1, Zn₄Ge₂S₈ 18.8, Ga₄Cu₂Ag₂S₈ 21.2 | **~18–22** |
| Selenide analogues of the same frameworks (Cd₂Ga₄Se₈ 41.7, Ga₄Hg₂Se₈ 72.7, Cu‑chalcopyrite selenides 45–55) | 40–75 |
| Tellurides, phosphides/arsenides, IV–VI (GeTe‑PbSe 302, Mg₄Ge₄As₈ 122) | 40–300 |
| **Li–Mg(Zn)–Ga–Se quaternaries (small cells)**: 16.7, 19.0, 19.3, 20.4, 21.5, 21.7, 22.5, 22.6, 25.1 … (mean ≈ 20) | **~17–25** |

Two "sweet‑spot" families therefore sit right at 20 pm/V: (i) **Zn/Cd/Hg–Ga–S defect chalcopyrites**, and (ii) **small‑cell Li–Mg–Ga–Se quaternaries**.

**Step 2 – Screening the pool**

* Discarded as too **large**: Cu‑ or Ag‑chalcopyrite selenides (c071, c056, c093 ≈ 40–55), Al₄Hg₂Se₈ (c082 ≈ 40, Se doubles the S value), CdSiP₂ (c030 ≈ 60–85), AlGaAs (c055 ≈ 80), CdInTeAs (c073 ≈ 80), Tl₉Sb₃S₉ (c038 ≈ 45, cf. Tl₉As₃S₉ 44.8), Li₄As₄S₈ (c083).
* Discarded as too **small**: all Rb/Cs/K halides and haloperovskite‑derived A₂MX₆/A₆M₆X₁₈ (c084–c086, c091, c059, c054, c023: 0.1–3), Na₂Sr₂B₂S₆ borosulfides (c040–c045 ≈ 5–10), LiAlS₂ (c057 ≈ 7), SiC polytypes (c024–c029 ≈ 7–13, cf. ZnS polytypes 15 scaled by the much smaller SiC polarizability), BeSe (c037 ≈ 10), Cs₈S₁₂/Cs₈Se₁₂, KLiZnS₂/RbLiZnS₂ (c046, c067), and the **pseudo‑cubic** Zn/Mg‑Ga‑chalcogenide (c050) — the near‑cubic MgGa₂Se₄ analogues in training collapse to ≈ 3 pm/V.
* Kept as ~20: the two genuine **ZnGa₂S₄ defect chalcopyrites** (c051, c052 — direct isostructural analogues of Cd₂Ga₄S₈ = 21.7; note Zn↔Cd barely changes d, cf. Zn₂Ga₄Te₈ 92.0 vs Cd₂Ga₄Te₈ 91.7), and the **compact Li₂MgGa₂Se₅ / Li₃Mg₂Ga₃Se₈** members whose Li:Mg:Ga:Se ratios and cell metrics interpolate between LiMgGaSe₃ (20–25) and Li₃Mg₂GaSe₅ (17–28).

**Step 3 – Estimates for the finalists**

| candidate | formula / motif | predicted |d| |
|---|---|---|
| c052 | ZnGa₂S₄ defect chalcopyrite (c/2a ≈ 1.04) | ≈ 21 |
| c095 | Li₂MgGa₂Se₅, cell 6.43/3.95/9.85 (≈ the 21.7 pm/V analogue) | ≈ 21 |
| c051 | ZnGa₂S₄ alternate vacancy ordering | ≈ 20 (19–20) |
| c097 | Li₂MgGa₂Se₅, cell 6.32/3.90/9.59 (≈ the 21.5 pm/V analogue) | ≈ 22 |
| c015 | Li₃Mg₂Ga₃Se₈, ordered chalcopyrite‑like 16‑atom cell | ≈ 23 |

(next in line: c014, c096, c048 YCuSe₂ ≈ 18–20, c021 ≈ 22)

**Final: c052, c095, c051, c097, c015**
